fixes.explanation: Yes, baker! The quote says, “But My righteous one will live by faith…” (Hebrews 10:38). Faith is the word it gives for how the righteous one lives. Plain and simple, friend.

Mount Sinai is a big mountain, but the writer never mentions it in this passage. The place he names is the Most Holy Place. Believers have confidence to enter it, he says, by the blood of Jesus (Hebrews 10:19). That's the place he's pointing to.

This one is actually true. The writer says the way is “…the new and living way opened for us through the curtain of His body…” (Hebrews 10:20). So it was opened for us through the curtain of Jesus' body. It's a new way, a living way, and it's already open, friend.

Fame and honor aren't what he's after. The writer says, “…spur one another on to love and good deeds.” (Hebrews 10:24). Love and good deeds are the destination he names. No spotlight on that list, friend.

That's it. The writer says, “Let us not neglect meeting together, as some have made a habit…” (Hebrews 10:25). Some had made neglecting it a habit. Instead he says, “…but let us encourage one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.” (Hebrews 10:25).

Money isn't mentioned in this warning, friend. The writer says some had made a habit of neglecting meeting together (Hebrews 10:25). The habit is about showing up, not about what's in the wallet. Right after, he points them toward encouraging one another.

Land isn't mentioned here, friend. The writer says that if we deliberately go on sinning after we have received the knowledge of the truth, “…no further sacrifice for sins remains…” (Hebrews 10:26). That condition matters, because it's about deliberately going on sinning. It's a heavy verse, so no worries about reading it twice.

Yes, baker. The writer says this person “…has trampled on the Son of God, profaned the blood of the covenant that sanctified him, and insulted the Spirit of grace?” (Hebrews 10:29). Notice the Son, the blood of the covenant and the Spirit of grace all show up in that one verse. It's serious business, friend.

Small isn't the word. The writer says, “It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.” (Hebrews 10:31). Just before that, he reminds them that God said He will repay and that the Lord will judge His people (Hebrews 10:30). Calling it small would shrink what he just said, friend.

Joyfully! The writer says they “…joyfully accepted the confiscation of your property…” (Hebrews 10:34). That's a hard thing to lose, and they met it with joy. The same verse says they were “…knowing that you yourselves had a better and permanent possession.”

Fearful would make sense to most of us, but that's not the word. The writer says they “…joyfully accepted the confiscation of your property…” (Hebrews 10:34). The same verse says they were “…knowing that you yourselves had a better and permanent possession.”
Not a burden, friend. The writer says, “So do not throw away your confidence; it holds a great reward.” (Hebrews 10:35). He says it holds a great reward, and that's why he says not to throw it away.

Yes, baker. The writer says, “You need to persevere, so that after you have done the will of God, you will receive what He has promised.” (Hebrews 10:36). Perseverance means sticking with it. Like pressing out the last cookie of a huge batch when your arm is tired.

Rest is a good thing, but it's not what the writer says here. He says, “You need to persevere, so that after you have done the will of God, you will receive what He has promised.” (Hebrews 10:36). He asks them to persevere, to keep going until they receive what He has promised. That's his word for the stretch before the promise, friend.

Repent isn't the word in this verse. The writer says, “You need to persevere, so that after you have done the will of God, you will receive what He has promised.” (Hebrews 10:36). He asks them to persevere, which means sticking with it. Notice the order: first they do the will of God, then they receive what He has promised.

The law is mentioned earlier in the passage, but not here. The quote says, “But My righteous one will live by faith…” (Hebrews 10:38). So the righteous one lives by faith. It then adds, “…and if he shrinks back, I will take no pleasure in him.”
